verses.1:1: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen sojourners of the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
verses.1:2: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to His great mercy has given us new birth to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
verses.1:4: to an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled, and unfading, preserved in the heavens for you,
verses.1:5: who are kept under guard by the power of God through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed at the last time.
verses.1:6: In this you exult, though for a little while now, if it is necessary, you have been grieved by manifold trials,
verses.1:7: that the proving of your faith—far more precious than gold that perishes, though it is proved by fire—may be found to yield praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:8: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, yet believing in Him, you exult with a joy beyond telling and filled with glory,
verses.1:9: obtaining the goal of your faith—the salvation of your souls.
verses.1:10: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who prophesied of the grace appointed for you searched intently and inquired diligently,
verses.1:11: searching out what time or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ in them was signifying, when He bore witness beforehand of the sufferings appointed for Christ and the glories that would follow.
verses.1:12: To them it was revealed that they were ministering these things not for themselves, but for you—things that have now been announced to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look.
verses.1:13: Therefore, having girded up the loins of your mind, being wholly sober-minded, set your hope upon the grace that is being brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
verses.1:14: As children of obedience, do not be fashioned according to the former lusts in your ignorance,
verses.1:15: but just as the Holy One who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all your conduct,
verses.1:16: for it is written, "You shall be holy, because I am holy."
verses.1:17: And if you call on Him as Father who judges impartially according to the work of each one, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your sojourning,
verses.1:18: knowing that it was not with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were redeemed from your vain manner of life handed down from your fathers,
verses.1:19: but with precious blood, as of an unblemished and spotless lamb—even of Christ,
verses.1:20: who was foreknown before the foundation of the world, yet was made manifest at the end of the times for your sake,
verses.1:21: who through Him believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and granted Him glory, so that your faith and hope are set on God.
verses.1:22: Having purified your souls in obedience to the truth for unfeigned brotherly love, love one another fervently from the heart,
verses.1:23: having been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the word of God that lives and abides;
verses.1:24: for, "All flesh is as grass, and all its glory as the blossom of the grass; the grass withers, and the blossom falls away,
verses.1:25: but the word of the Lord abides forever." And this is the very word that was proclaimed to you as the gospel.
verses.2:1: Therefore, putting off all malice and all guile, hypocrisies, envies, and all slanders,
verses.2:2: as newborn babes, earnestly desire the unadulterated spiritual milk, that by it you may grow up into salvation,
verses.2:3: if you have tasted that the Lord is good.
verses.2:4: As you draw near to Him—a living stone, rejected by men indeed, yet chosen and precious in the sight of God—
verses.2:5: you yourselves also, as living stones, are being built up into a spiritual house for a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
verses.2:6: For it is contained in Scripture: "Behold, I lay in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious; and he who believes in Him shall never be put to shame."
verses.2:7: To you therefore who believe belongs this honor; yet to those who disbelieve, "The stone that the builders rejected, that very stone has become the head of the corner,"
verses.2:8: and, "A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense." They stumble, disobeying the word—to which they were also appointed.
verses.2:9: But you are a chosen lineage, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for His possession, that you may declare the excellencies of Him who called you out of darkness into His wondrous light;
verses.2:10: who formerly were not a people, yet now are the people of God; who had not been shown mercy, yet now have been shown mercy.
verses.2:11: Beloved, I exhort you as aliens and sojourners to abstain from fleshly passions, which wage war against the soul,
verses.2:12: keeping your conduct noble among the Gentiles, so that in the very matter in which they speak evil of you as wrongdoers, beholding your good works they may glorify God in the day of visitation.
verses.2:13: Be subject to every human institution for the sake of the Lord, whether to the king as holding supreme authority,
verses.2:14: or to governors as those sent by him for the punishment of wrongdoers and the commendation of those who do good
verses.2:15: (for such is the will of God, that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men);
verses.2:16: as free people, yet not holding your liberty as a cover for malice, but as bondservants of God.
verses.2:17: Show honor to everyone; love the brotherhood; fear God; pay honor to the king.
verses.2:18: Household servants, be subject to your masters in all reverence, not only to those who are good and considerate, but also to those who are perverse.
verses.2:19: For this is grace, if on account of conscience toward God one bears up under sorrows while suffering unjustly.
verses.2:20: For what credit is it if you sin and are buffeted and endure it? Yet if, while doing good and suffering, you endure, this is grace before God.
verses.2:21: For to this very end you were called, because Christ also suffered on your behalf, leaving you a pattern so that you might follow in His footsteps;
verses.2:22: who did no sin, neither was any guile found in His mouth;
verses.2:23: who, being reviled, did not revile in return; while suffering, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to the One who judges justly;
verses.2:24: He Himself bore our sins in His body upon the tree, so that having died to sins, we might live to righteousness; by His wound you were healed.
verses.2:25: For you were straying as sheep, yet now you have turned back to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
verses.3:1: In like manner, wives, be subject to your own husbands, so that even if any do not obey the word, through the manner of life of their wives they shall be won without a word,
verses.3:2: as they behold your pure conduct in reverent fear.
verses.3:3: Do not let your adornment be the outward one—the braiding of hair, the wearing of gold ornaments, or the putting on of garments—
verses.3:4: but rather the hidden person of the heart, in the imperishable grace of a meek and quiet spirit, which is of great value in the sight of God.
verses.3:5: For thus in times past the holy women who hoped in God also adorned themselves, submitting themselves to their own husbands,
verses.3:6: just as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him "lord"; whose children you have become, doing good and not fearing any terror.
verses.3:7: Husbands, in like manner, dwell with them according to knowledge, bestowing honor upon the woman as the weaker vessel, as also to co-heirs of the grace of life, in order that your prayers may not be hindered.
verses.3:8: Finally, all of you, be harmonious in mind, compassionate, loving the brethren, tenderhearted, and humble-minded,
verses.3:9: not rendering evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but rather giving a blessing, for to this very purpose you were called, so that you might inherit a blessing.
verses.3:10: For, "He who wishes to love life and behold good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking guile;
verses.3:11: let him turn aside from evil and do what is good; let him search for peace and pursue it.
verses.3:12: For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears are attentive to their supplication; yet the face of the Lord is against those who practice evil."
verses.3:13: And who is the one who will do you harm if you become zealous for that which is good?
verses.3:14: Yet even if you should suffer on account of righteousness, blessed are you. Do not fear their threats, nor be troubled,
verses.3:15: but in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord, always prepared to offer a defense to anyone who asks of you a reason concerning the hope within you,
verses.3:16: yet with meekness and reverence, maintaining a good conscience, so that in whatever matter you are spoken against, those who malign your good manner of life in Christ may be put to shame.
verses.3:17: For it is better to suffer while doing good, if the will of God should so desire, than while doing evil.
verses.3:18: For Christ also died once for sins, the righteous on behalf of the unrighteous, so that He might lead you to God—put to death indeed in the flesh, yet made alive in the spirit;
verses.3:19: in which also He went and made proclamation to the spirits in prison,
verses.3:20: who once were disobedient, when the longsuffering of God waited expectantly in the days of Noah, while an ark was being constructed, into which a few—that is, eight souls—were safely delivered through water.
verses.3:21: Corresponding to this, baptism now saves you also—not the putting off of the filth of the flesh, but the appeal of a good conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
verses.3:22: who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, with angels, authorities, and powers subjected to Him.
verses.4:1: Therefore, since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves likewise with the same resolve, for the one who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sin,
verses.4:2: so as to live the remaining time in the flesh no longer for the desires of men, but for the will of God.
verses.4:3: For the time already past is sufficient to have carried out the desire of the Gentiles, having walked in debauchery, lusts, drunkenness, revelries, drinking bouts, and lawless idolatries.
verses.4:4: In this they are astonished that you do not run together with them into the same flood of dissipation, reviling you;
verses.4:5: who shall render an account to Him who stands ready to judge the living and the dead.
verses.4:6: For to this end the gospel was proclaimed even to the dead, that they might be judged according to men in the flesh, yet live according to God in the spirit.
verses.4:7: Now the end of all things has drawn near. Therefore be of sound judgment and sober-minded for prayers.
verses.4:8: Above all, maintain earnest love among yourselves, because love covers a multitude of sins.
verses.4:9: Offer hospitality to one another without murmuring.
verses.4:10: Even as each has received a gift of grace, use it in serving one another as good stewards of the varied grace of God.
verses.4:11: If anyone speaks, let it be as the oracles of God; if anyone serves, let it be from the strength that God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the might forever and ever. Amen.
verses.4:12: Beloved, do not be astonished at the fiery ordeal coming upon you for your testing, as though some strange thing were befalling you,
verses.4:13: but insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that at the revelation of His glory you may also rejoice with exultant gladness.
verses.4:14: If you are reviled in the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests upon you.
verses.4:15: For let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evildoer, or as a meddler in the affairs of others;
verses.4:16: yet if someone suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; rather, let him glorify God in this name.
verses.4:17: For the season has arrived for judgment to begin at the household of God; and if it begins first with us, what shall be the end of those who disobey the gospel of God?
verses.4:18: And if the righteous one is saved with difficulty, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?
verses.4:19: Therefore let those also who suffer according to the will of God commend their souls to a faithful Creator in doing good.
verses.5:1: Therefore I exhort the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a partaker also of the glory about to be revealed:
verses.5:2: shepherd the flock of God that is among you, not under compulsion but willingly, according to God; neither for shameful gain, but with eagerness;
verses.5:3: nor as domineering over those allotted to your charge, but becoming examples to the flock.
verses.5:4: And when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, you shall receive the unfading crown of glory.
verses.5:5: Likewise, you younger ones, submit yourselves to the elders. Moreover, all of you, gird yourselves with humility toward one another, because "God resists the proud, yet gives grace to the humble."
verses.5:6: Humble yourselves, therefore, beneath the mighty hand of God, so that He may exalt you at the appointed time,
verses.5:7: casting all your anxious care upon Him, because He cares for you.
verses.5:8: Be sober-minded, keep watch. Your adversary the devil goes about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
verses.5:9: Withstand him, steadfast in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being fulfilled among your brotherhood in the world.
verses.5:10: Now the God of all grace, who called you into His eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered for a little while, shall Himself restore, establish, strengthen, and ground you.
verses.5:11: To Him belongs the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
verses.5:12: Through Silvanus, whom I reckon a faithful brother, I have written to you in few words, exhorting and bearing witness that this is the true grace of God; stand fast in it.
verses.5:13: She who is in Babylon, chosen along with you, greets you, as does Mark, my son.
verses.5:14: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace be with all of you who are in Christ.

notes.1:11: Greek eis tina e poion kairon may be rendered either "what time or what manner of time" (taking both interrogatives with kairon) or "what person or what time."
notes.1:12: The critical Greek text reads "for you" (hymin) rather than "for us" (hemin), emphasizing that the Old Testament prophets ministered for the benefit of the epistle's recipients.
notes.1:13: The adverb teleios ("wholly") is punctuated here with the preceding participle ("being wholly sober-minded"), though many interpreters connect it with the imperative ("set your hope completely").
notes.1:22: The critical Greek text reads simply "from the heart" (ek kardias), without the later manuscript expansions "through the Spirit" and "a pure heart."
notes.2:2: Greek logikon carries the senses "spiritual" and "reasonable" (or "of the word"). The critical Greek text includes the concluding phrase "into salvation" (eis soterian), which is absent from the later Byzantine tradition.
notes.2:7: The critical Greek text reads "to those who disbelieve" (apistousin) rather than "to those who are disobedient" (apeithousin).
notes.2:19: Greek charis here denotes "grace" in the sense of divine favor or commendation; syneidesin theou ("conscience toward God") expresses a reverent mindfulness of God.
notes.2:21: The critical Greek text reads "on your behalf, leaving you" (hyper hymon, hymin) rather than "for us, leaving us."
notes.3:15: The critical Greek text reads "Christ as Lord" (kyrion de ton Christon) rather than "the Lord God" (kyrion de ton theon), applying the language of Isaiah 8:13 directly to Christ.
notes.3:18: The critical Greek text reads "died" (apethanen) and "lead you" (hymas) rather than "suffered" and "us." The dative pneumati ("in the spirit") is debated, referring either to the spiritual realm of Christ's resurrection life or to His being made alive by the Holy Spirit.
notes.3:19: The identity of "the spirits in prison" and the timing of Christ's proclamation are much debated, with interpreters viewing them as rebellious angelic spirits (cf. Gen 6:1-4; 2 Pet 2:4), the disobedient generation of Noah's day, or those to whom Christ preached through Noah in the Spirit.
notes.3:21: Greek eperotema can mean "appeal," "pledge," or "inquiry," contrasting an inward moral appeal or commitment to God with mere outward bodily washing.
notes.4:6: Commentators debate whether 'the dead' refers to believers who heard the gospel during their lifetimes and have since died, or to the spirits of the dead in the realm of the dead (compare 3:19).
notes.4:14: Later Byzantine manuscripts add 'on their part He is blasphemed, but on your part He is glorified,' which is absent from the earliest Greek witnesses.
notes.4:15: The rare Greek noun allotriepiskopos occurs only here in the New Testament and denotes an unauthorized overseer of another's affairs, meaning a meddler or busybody.
notes.4:16: The critical Greek text reads 'in this name' (en to onomati touto), referring to the name 'Christian,' whereas later manuscripts read 'in this matter' (en to merei touto).
notes.5:2: The critical Greek text omits 'serving as overseers' (episkopountes) and includes 'according to God' (kata theon), both of which vary across ancient manuscripts.
notes.5:5: The rare verb enkomboomai literally means to tie on a garment, evoking a servant girding on an apron of humility; the quotation is drawn from Proverbs 3:34 in the Septuagint.
notes.5:12: The critical Greek text reads the imperative 'stand fast' (stete) rather than the indicative 'you stand' (hestekate) found in later manuscripts.
notes.5:13: 'She who is in Babylon' is widely understood as a figurative reference to the church in Rome, using 'Babylon' as a symbolic designation for the imperial capital.
